label: D2 step late in the episode (episode-clock unit)
explanation: Fires only at D2 (100% of mass) and only in the last ~25 trials of the 100-trial episode: zero activations before trial 50, 2.6% of steps in trials 70-79, 17% in 80-89, 30% in 90-99. It acts as an episode-time / end-of-episode signal and is correspondingly anti-correlated with the value head (79% of mass at value < 5.22; value falls as the episode nears its end). Never fires at D1 or GO, or when a reward input is shown. Magnitude grows with episode trial and is larger after choosing a2 (in_action == 2 holds 75% of mass); rare transitions give the top activations, but the transition and reward history have little effect on the firing rate. Recorded (phase == D2) & (ep_trial >= 85) (dev F1 0.815, mass recall 0.93); a variant that admits a2 trials from trial 80 reaches F1 0.84, and (phase == D2) & (value < 6.5) gives F1 0.83. Only observed variables are used (the episode clock is implicit in the recurrent state).

issues: The factual claims check out on dev. 100% of activation mass is at D2, with zero activity at D1 and GO. The unit never fires before trial 50 (44 steps in trials 50-59, 408 in 60-69). Firing rates are 2.6% in trials 70-79, 16.9% in 80-89 and 30.3% in 90-99. 79.4% of the mass is at value < 5.22. in_action==2 holds 74.9% of the mass. 'Never when a reward input is shown' is true but follows trivially from D2-only firing, so it is not an independent finding.

Recorded predicate reproduces on test: P 0.833, R 0.828, F1 0.831, mass recall 0.940. Missed steps hold only 6% of the mass, and coverage by activation quartile is 0.51, 0.82, 0.98 and 1.00. So the misses are mostly the weakest activations, from the ramp-up in trials ~70-84.

The explanation understates how much the choice modulates firing. Within D2 at ep_trial >= 85, precision is 0.94 after a2 and 0.66 after a1. a2 & good==2 gives 0.976, while a1 & good==1 gives 0.647, so it is the action (not the good state) that drives this. The policy logit also gates it: at late D2 with choice (logit a1 - a2) >= 2.78, precision is only 0.168. The unit is an episode clock whose threshold is lower when the agent is choosing or leaning toward a2. That is a systematic modulation, though a fairly small one in F1 terms.

Transition and reward history are only weak modulators, so the claim that they barely matter holds roughly. Late-D2 precision is 0.84 for common vs 0.76 for rare transitions, and stay vs switch makes little difference.

Refined predicates beat the recorded one only slightly on test. (phase == D2) & (ep_trial >= 82) & (choice < 2) gets F1 0.858 and mass recall 0.963. (phase == D2) & ((ep_trial >= 88) | ((ep_trial >= 80) & (action == 2))) & (choice < 2.5) gets F1 0.857. Misses for the refined predicate are scattered weak ramp-onset activations with no remaining systematic class. Both refined predicates use only observed variables plus the model's own policy logit.
